Robot Framework is an open-source, **keyword-driven** automation framework. You
write checks as sequences of named actions — keywords like `Log` or
`Should Be Equal` — and libraries teach the framework new keywords. The same
syntax serves **test automation**, **robotic process automation (RPA)**, and
**synthetic monitoring**.

Its home ground is **acceptance- and system-level** verification: whole
workflows across real interfaces — a web page, an API, a file on disk — not the
individual functions inside your code. That is what makes a check read like a
procedure a whole team can follow.

Three ideas anchor everything that follows:

1. **Keyword-driven** — every check is built from keywords, human-readable by
   design.
2. **Acceptance- and system-level** — it verifies whole workflows across
   interfaces, not units of code.
3. **Generic** — one syntax for test automation, RPA, and synthetic monitoring.

> **Note:** Robot Framework is stewarded by the Robot Framework Foundation and
> released under the Apache License 2.0 — free to use, and free to extend with
> your own libraries.

> **Tip:** When you meet a new keyword later, read its name first. A good
> Robot Framework check often reads top-to-bottom like plain instructions.

> **Warning:** Robot Framework is not a unit-testing tool. Reaching for it to
> test a single function in isolation is the most common early misstep — use it
> where whole workflows meet.
